articles.title: Where to support flood relief in Kathmandu this week and beyond
articles.summary: The article lists a series of events taking place in Kathmandu this week and beyond that allow residents and visitors to contribute to flood relief efforts. Options include charity runs, creative workshops, donation drives, and community gatherings organized by local NGOs, the Kathmandu Metropolitan City, and international aid groups. Each event provides details on dates, locations, and how participants can donate or volunteer, aiming to support flood‑affected families with food, shelter, and rebuilding supplies.

articles.title: This Nepali film won at Cannes. Here’s what makes it stand out
articles.summary: Abinash Bikram Shah’s film 'Elephants in the Fog' (Tiniharu) has won an award at the Cannes Film Festival, marking a historic achievement for Nepali cinema. The movie centers on a Kinnar (transgender) family, exploring themes of belonging, othering, and the delicate limits of societal acceptance. Critics praise its nuanced storytelling, visual style, and the way it brings marginalized voices to an international stage, highlighting Nepal’s growing cultural footprint.

articles.title: 27 US lawmakers urge Rubio to expand rescue, aid efforts in Nepal
articles.summary: Following a major disaster in Nepal that left thousands missing, a group of 27 U.S. lawmakers have written to Senator Marco Rubio urging the expansion of American rescue and aid operations. The legislators request the deployment of a U.S. disaster response team, the provision of high‑altitude search and rescue assets, and a faster overall assistance effort to support Nepalese authorities. They emphasize the urgent need for additional resources to locate missing persons and provide humanitarian relief, highlighting the severity of the situation and the importance of a coordinated international response.

articles.title: Nepal PM Balendra Shah to address UN General Assembly on September 24
articles.summary: Prime Minister Balendra Shah will make his first foreign trip since taking office to address the United Nations General Assembly on September 24. The appearance comes as Nepal reels from catastrophic floods that have caused extensive damage and loss of life. The PM hopes to draw international attention and secure aid and support for relief and reconstruction efforts. The upcoming speech highlights Nepal's urgent need for global assistance and marks a significant diplomatic engagement for the newly elected government.

articles.title: Nepal flood death toll reaches 1,342
articles.summary: The death toll from recent floods in Nepal has risen to 1,342. Police report that 4,886 people remain missing and 1,030 bodies have already been buried. Search and rescue operations are ongoing across the affected regions as authorities confront the scale of the disaster.

articles.title: NEPSE falls as flood concerns weigh on insurance, hydropower
articles.summary: The Nepal Stock Exchange (NEPSE) slipped 0.57% over a four‑session week, wiping out roughly Rs30 billion in market value. Weak momentum and thin trading kept the index near key support levels, with flood concerns dampening outlooks for the insurance and hydropower sectors, which are significant components of the market.

articles.title: Chinese national pulled alive from hydropower tunnel in Nepal after 10 days
articles.summary: A Chinese worker named Luhaitao was rescued alive after being trapped for ten days inside the Upper Trishuli‑1 hydropower tunnel in Nepal. Rescuers, including Nepali and foreign teams, located him about 225 metres into the tunnel and successfully extracted him, marking the end of an intensive search operation.

articles.title: Where rescue efforts stand at flood-hit hydropower projects
articles.summary: Rescue teams continue searching flooded tunnels and damaged hydropower sites in Nepal after severe floods. Two workers have been rescued and several bodies recovered, but hundreds of people remain missing. The ongoing operation highlights the challenges of accessing submerged infrastructure and the urgent need for coordinated relief efforts.

articles.title: Woman rescued alive after 10 days trapped in debris-buried house
articles.summary: A 64‑year‑old woman, Chandika Kumari Shrestha, was rescued alive after being trapped for ten days beneath debris in a four‑storey house that collapsed in Betrawati, Nepal. An Armed Police Force rescue team located her on the upper floor and successfully extricated her, bringing her to safety. The incident highlights ongoing concerns about building safety and the effectiveness of emergency response teams in the region.

articles.title: Two people rescued alive on 11th day after floods
articles.summary: On the 11th day after severe floods in Nepal, two individuals were rescued alive. A Chinese national was pulled from a hydropower tunnel in Rasuwa district, while a 64‑year‑old woman was rescued from the upper floor of a house in Nuwakot district. The rescues highlight ongoing relief efforts as communities continue to recover from the disaster.

articles.title: Security personnel install Nepali flag on the border with China in Rasuwagadhi
articles.summary: Security personnel installed the Nepali flag on the border with China in Rasuwagadhi after the settlement was swept away by devastating floods, leaving no clear separation between the two territories.

articles.title: Nepal wants to be a clean-energy powerhouse. The indigenous people are paying the price
articles.summary: Nepal is pursuing an aggressive hydropower expansion backed by billions in financing, aiming to become a clean‑energy powerhouse. However, indigenous communities say they were not consulted and are bearing the environmental and social costs of the projects, leading to protests and concerns over rights and consent.

articles.title: Two killed in landslide at Super Seti hydropower project
articles.summary: A landslide struck the under-construction Super Seti hydropower project in Kaski district on Saturday, killing two workers who were digging a road at the site. The incident highlights safety concerns at large infrastructure projects in Nepal.

articles.title: Floods revive questions over an abandoned mountain airstrip
articles.summary: Recent floods in the Langtang region have reignited debate over the abandoned Langtang Airport, a high‑altitude airstrip at 3,658 metres. While the runway has been out of service for years, the disaster highlighted its potential role in delivering relief supplies and evacuating victims from remote mountain communities. Government officials, tourism authorities, and local residents are weighing the costs of refurbishing the airstrip against safety concerns and environmental impact. Proponents argue that a functional airport could boost tourism and improve emergency response, while critics cite the high maintenance expenses and the risk of triggering further ecological disturbance. The discussion comes amid broader national conversations on infrastructure resilience and disaster preparedness in Nepal’s mountainous zones.

articles.title: Flood-displaced mothers struggle for privacy and care
articles.summary: Following recent floods in Nepal, many pregnant women and new mothers have been forced into crowded shelters where they lack privacy, sufficient food, and access to essential maternity care. Damaged roads have isolated these shelters from nearby hospitals, worsening the situation for the displaced families.

articles.title: Late rescues renew hope for survivors in deadly Nepal floods
articles.summary: Late rescues have sparked renewed hope among survivors of Nepal's deadly floods. A 64-year-old woman was pulled alive from beneath her collapsed home while her family was performing her death rites. Additionally, three people, including a Chinese national, were rescued from flooded hydropower tunnels in Rasuwa district.

articles.title: Nepal’s economic growth suffers from a lack of vision
articles.summary: The article argues that Nepal’s recent economic growth figures are misleading because they do not reflect how growth is being generated or who benefits from it. It highlights structural weaknesses such as inadequate long‑term planning, poor investment in productive sectors, and uneven distribution of wealth. The author calls for a clear national vision, better policy coordination, and reforms to ensure that growth translates into broad‑based prosperity rather than limited gains for a few.

articles.title: Who holds Nepal’s energy switch now?
articles.summary: After years of chronic load‑shedding, Nepal announced an end to daily power cuts, crediting reforms in the Nepal Electricity Authority and stronger political will. However, the recent drop in river levels—especially in the Koshi and Trishuli basins—has sharply reduced hydro‑electric generation, the backbone of the country’s grid. With reservoirs low and monsoon rains delayed, the government faces renewed shortages, prompting emergency imports and calls for diversified energy sources. Energy Minister Shishir Khanal warned that without sustained water flow, the gains of better governance could be undone, while Prime Minister Pushpa Kamal Dahal urged accelerated investment in solar and wind projects. The article highlights the fragile balance between governance reforms and Nepal’s reliance on seasonal river water for power.

articles.title: Panel formed to conduct PNDA has six weeks to prepare report
articles.summary: The government has set up a panel to conduct a Post‑Disaster Needs Assessment (PNDA) with a six‑week deadline to produce its report. A Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment estimates that the August 26 flood caused roughly Rs 400 billion in damage.

articles.title: Nepal is draining four glacial lakes. Scientists say it is not enough
articles.summary: The Nepalese government is actively draining four glacial lakes to reduce the threat of catastrophic floods. Experts warn that while this effort is a step forward, it alone will not be sufficient. They stress the need for comprehensive risk assessments, robust early warning systems, proper outlet management, and careful construction practices in flood‑prone zones to effectively mitigate potential disasters.

articles.title: Kathmandu supply lines rerouted after floods block main highway
articles.summary: Heavy floods have blocked the main highway leading into Kathmandu, forcing supply routes for fuel, food and other essentials to be diverted to alternative roads. While the capital continues to receive basic goods, the disruption has caused price hikes and limited the availability of cooking gas. Authorities are working to clear the blockage and restore normal logistics, but residents face rising costs and uncertainty as the floodwaters recede.

articles.title: Kremlin says Ukraine talks with US envoys were useful; no sign of breakthrough
articles.summary: The Kremlin said recent talks between Ukrainian officials and U.S. envoys were useful, but acknowledged no breakthrough in resolving the conflict. President Vladimir Putin praised former U.S. President Donald Trump’s past efforts to end the war, yet highlighted that major disagreements remain over territorial issues and Ukraine’s future security. The discussions, while deemed constructive, did not produce any concrete settlement, leaving the war’s resolution still uncertain.

articles.title: Flood damages four houses and bridge in Gorkha
articles.summary: A pre-dawn flood struck the remote Chumnubri Rural Municipality in Gorkha district, Nepal, destroying four houses and sweeping away a bridge. No casualties were reported.

articles.title: Reporter’s Diary: I went back to Rasuwa. The river had changed everything
articles.summary: Fourteen months after reporting on the initial Lhende Khola flood in Rasuwa district, the journalist returns to find the landscape dramatically altered. Roads have vanished, homes are destroyed, and families are still searching for missing loved ones. The article recounts the lingering devastation, the challenges of recovery, and the emotional impact on residents who struggle to recognize the places they once knew.

articles.title: Scan, tap, done: How digital payments are changing disaster relief in Nepal
articles.summary: The article examines how Nepal's adoption of mobile banking and QR code payments has transformed disaster relief efforts. A decade after the 2015 earthquake, these digital tools enabled the rapid collection of over Rs10 billion for flood victims within days, streamlining aid distribution and reducing reliance on cash. The piece highlights the benefits of faster, more transparent transactions, while also noting challenges such as digital literacy and infrastructure gaps that need to be addressed to fully leverage the technology in future emergencies.
